mainTopic: רב and רבי יוחנן on מעילה in ashes on the מזבח, and רב and לוי on where מעילה repayment money goes
overview: The amud opens by testing the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן about ashes left on top of the מזבח. רב says there is no מעילה in them, and רבי יוחנן says there still is. The test is a משנה that says a coal (גחלת) which fell off the מזבח is not put back. In one version, the משנה implies that a coal still on the מזבח must be put back, which challenges רב. רב answers that a coal is different because it has substance (מששא). In a second version, the same משנה seems to say that ash has no מעילה, which challenges רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה mentions a coal to teach a bigger חידוש. The גמרא then brings a new argument between רב and לוי about where the money paid for מעילה goes. רב says it goes to gift offerings, and לוי says it buys something burned entirely on the מזבח, which is קטורת. Each side has a ברייתא supporting it. The ברייתא that supports רב seems to contradict itself. The גמרא explains that its first part follows רבי שמעון, who holds that a חטאת whose owner already got atonement is left to die.

steps.title: A משנה about things that fell off the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: things that fell off the מזבח, including a coal, are not put back. It infers that a coal still on the מזבח must be put back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a משנה: All those items that fell off the altar should not be put back. Likewise, a coal that fell off the altar should not be put back. This implies that if it is still on the altar, it should be put back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and draws an inference from it. This is the setup for a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a coal which fell off the מזבח is not returned. The גמרא reads it from the other side: if a coal slipped but is still on top of the מזבח, it still belongs to the מזבח, so he must put it back on the fire. That suggests the material on top of the מזבח keeps its holy status.

keyTerms.meaning: jumped off, were dislodged
he should not put it back
a burning coal or ember
the altar

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: וְכוּלָּן, שֶׁפָּקְעוּ מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ – לֹא יַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: They challenged: And all of them that were dislodged from upon the altar, he should not put back,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the unfit offerings that, once they're up on the מזבח, don't get taken down. This comes from זבחים פו.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן גַּחֶלֶת שֶׁפָּקְעָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ – לֹא יַחֲזִיר.
phrases.english: And likewise, a coal that was dislodged from upon the altar, he should not put back.
This implies: if it is on the altar, he should put it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the earlier argument between רב and רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the ashes on the מזבח no longer have holy status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a coal still on the מזבח must be put back, then what sits on the מזבח keeps its status.

steps.title: The inference fits רבי יוחנן but not רב
steps.stepSummary: The inference works well for רבי יוחנן but is difficult for רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי יוחנן it works out well. But according to רב, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out who is bothered by the משנה's inference: it fits רבי יוחנן and challenges רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that whatever is still on the מזבח keeps its holiness, so a coal on the מזבח must be put back. רב said this material had lost its status, so why would a coal still on the מזבח need to be put back?

keyTerms.meaning: granted, it makes sense
it works out well
it is difficult, a challenge

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, it works out well,
but according to Rav, it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַב, קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the challenge that comes out of the inference in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that a coal on the מזבח still belongs to it, which goes against רב.

steps.title: רב answers that a coal is different
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that a coal is different because it still has real substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could say to you: A coal is different, because it has substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends himself by saying the משנה is only talking about a coal, which is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coal is still solid and can still burn, so it still counts as something for the מזבח. Ash that is fully burned has no substance. That is why רב can say a coal must be put back and still hold there is no מעילה in ash.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different
substance, something real and solid

phrases.english: Rav could say to you: A coal is different,
since it has substance.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a coal versus ash
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that everything on the מזבח keeps its status, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a coal, which has substance, keeps its status. Ash does not.

steps.title: Second version: the same משנה challenges רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Another version flips the inference. Since the משנה stresses that a coal has substance, ash would have no מעילה even on the מזבח. That fits רב and challenges רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it the other way: the reason is because it is a coal, which has substance. This implies that ash, which has no substance, has no מעילה even on top of the altar. Granted, according to רב it works out well, but according to רבי יוחנן it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion. Here the same משנה is used to challenge רבי יוחנן instead of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the reason "it has substance" is read as the whole point of the משנה. If only a coal counts, then ash on the מזבח does not count, and there is no מעילה in it. That is exactly רב's view and against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: there is one who says it differently, a second version
in the other direction
ash
there is no מעילה (the sin of using holy property for oneself)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. They are not two separate challenges. They are two ways of reporting the same discussion, and each one reads the משנה in the opposite direction.

phrases.english: There is one who says it in the other direction:

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא מִשּׁוּם גַּחֶלֶת, דְּאִית בַּיהּ מְשָׁשָׁא,
phrases.english: The reason is because it is a coal, which has substance;
this implies that ash, which has no substance,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ – אֵין מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: even on top of the altar, there is no misuse of it.
phrases.notes: "Misuse" here is מעילה, using holy property for yourself.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav, it works out well,
but according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version that uses the same משנה against the other side
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that there is מעילה in ash still on the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only a coal counts because it has substance, then ash on the מזבח has no status, so there is no מעילה in it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה teaches even a coal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that ash is the same. The משנה mentions a coal to teach that even a coal, which has substance, is not put back once it falls off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could say to you: The same is true even of ash. The reason the משנה mentions a coal is to teach us that even a coal, which has substance, is not put back once it falls off the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why the משנה chose to talk about a coal, without accepting that ash is any different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's real point is about falling off: something that fell off the מזבח is not returned. Saying this about a coal is the bigger חידוש, because you might have thought a solid coal should be put back. So the coal was not chosen to exclude ash.

keyTerms.meaning: the same law applies
to teach us something new

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the answer is the same kind of move: explain why the משנה used the word "coal." רב says a coal is a special case. רבי יוחנן says a coal is the bigger חידוש, and ash is the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you:
The same is true even of ash,
and this is the reason it teaches a coal:
it comes to teach us that even a coal,
which has substance,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פָּקְעָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ – לֹא יַחֲזִיר.
phrases.english: when it is dislodged from upon the altar, he should not put it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ אֵפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן in the second version
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading why the משנה chose the word "coal": it is the bigger חידוש, not a limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה mentions a coal to exclude ash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ash is the same. The coal is mentioned to teach that even something with substance is not put back once it falls off.

steps.title: רב and לוי argue about where the repayment money goes
steps.stepSummary: A person benefited from meat of a קדשי קדשים offering before the blood was sprinkled, or from the fats of a קדשים קלים offering after the blood was sprinkled. רב says the money he pays goes to gift offerings. לוי says it buys something that is entirely for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Someone benefited from the meat of a most-holy offering before its blood was sprinkled, or from the altar parts of a lesser-holy offering after its blood was sprinkled. רב says: the value of what he benefited goes to gift offerings. לוי says: he must bring something that goes entirely onto the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a dispute between רב and לוי about what happens to the money someone pays after committing מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are times when the item still fully belongs to the holy side, so using it is מעילה. Everyone agrees the person pays. The only question is what that money buys: general gift offerings (רב), or only something burned completely on the מזבח (לוי).

keyTerms.meaning: Most-holy offerings, such as a חטאת or עולה
Offerings of lesser holiness, such as a שלמים
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the key step of the offering
The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח, like the fats
Gift offerings; here, communal offerings bought from extra money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. For קדשי קדשים, the problem is the meat before the blood is sprinkled. For קדשים קלים, the problem is the altar parts after the blood is sprinkled.

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who benefits from the meat of most-holy offerings
before the sprinkling of the blood,
or from the altar parts of lesser-holy offerings
after the sprinkling of the blood,
רב says: the value of what he benefited
goes to gift offerings.
And לוי says:
He must bring something that goes entirely to the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It is not tied to the earlier discussion about the coal and the ash.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the money from מעילה goes to communal gift offerings. לוי: it must buy something burned entirely on the מזבח.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports לוי: the money buys קטורת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks where מעילה money goes. The answer is something entirely for the מזבח, which is קטורת, just as לוי said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with לוי: Where does this מעילה money go? Those who learn before the חכמים say: he brings something entirely for the altar. What is that? קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what לוי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same words as לוי: "something that goes entirely to the altar." It then names what that is: קטורת, which is burned completely. This gives לוי's view a source from the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Using holy property for oneself; the person must pay it back
"Those who learn before the חכמים", a name for a certain group of תנאים
Incense, which is burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with לוי:
This מעילה money, where does it go?
Those who learn before the חכמים say:
He must bring something that goes entirely to the altar.
What is that? Incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports the second opinion in the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: לוי's view that מעילה money buys something burned entirely on the מזבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from "those who learn before the חכמים", which names קטורת

steps.title: A ברייתא for רב begins: money of a חטאת and an אשם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that supports רב opens with money set aside for a חטאת or an אשם. If the offering was not brought yet, the money goes toward that offering. If it was already brought, חטאת money is thrown into the ים המלח, and אשם money goes to gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב: Someone benefited from money set aside for a חטאת or for an אשם. If his חטאת was not yet offered, he adds the money and brings his חטאת. If his אשם was not yet offered, he adds the money and brings his אשם. If his חטאת was already offered, the money goes to the ים המלח. If his אשם was already offered, the money goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that supports רב. This first part sets things up, and the line that clearly matches רב comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the offering is still waiting to be brought, the repaid money just goes back to buying it. Once it is brought, the two differ. Leftover חטאת money must be destroyed (thrown into the ים המלח), but leftover אשם money goes to gift offerings, the same place רב sends it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering
A guilt offering
He adds the money he repays to the original money
The Dead Sea; sending money there means it is destroyed and no one uses it

phrases.english: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב:
One who benefits from money for a sin offering or money for a guilt offering,
if his sin offering was not yet offered,
he adds the money and brings his sin offering.
And if his guilt offering was not yet offered,
he adds the money and brings his guilt offering.
If his sin offering was already offered, the money goes to the Dead Sea.
If his guilt offering was already offered, it goes to gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the support for לוי, the גמרא now brings a ברייתא that supports רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that מעילה money goes to gift offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about money set aside for a חטאת and an אשם

steps.title: The ברייתא rules on the very same case: the money goes to gift offerings
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא takes up the exact case that רב and לוי argued about and rules that the money goes to gift offerings, just as רב said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone benefited from most-holy offerings before the blood was sprinkled, or from the altar parts of lesser-holy offerings after the blood was sprinkled: the value of what he benefited goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the line that clearly supports רב. The ברייתא repeats the case of our dispute word for word and gives רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 was only a related case about חטאת and אשם money. This line is the exact case of the dispute, and its ruling, "goes to gift offerings," is רב's wording. So רב also has a ברייתא behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: The value of the benefit he got, which he has to pay back
Literally "they fall"; here, the money is assigned to that use

phrases.english: One who benefits from most-holy offerings
before the sprinkling of the blood,
or from the altar parts of lesser-holy offerings
after the sprinkling of the blood,
the value of what he benefited goes to gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִקׇּדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 8 and reaches the line that matches רב exactly.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that in this exact case the money goes to gift offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא repeats the exact case and uses רב's own words, "יפלו לנדבה"
steps.whyThisMatters: Each side of the dispute now has a ברייתא supporting it, so the disagreement goes back to the תנאים.

steps.title: The ברייתא's general rule: the money goes back to the same kind of holiness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a general rule. מעילה money from altar offerings goes to the מזבח. Money from things given for Temple upkeep goes to Temple upkeep. Money from communal offerings goes to communal gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: All altar offerings: the money goes to the altar. Things given for Temple upkeep: the money goes to Temple upkeep. Communal offerings: the money goes to communal gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with a general summary of where repayment money goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is simple: the money goes back to the same kind of holiness it was taken from. Altar things go back to the altar, Temple-upkeep things go back to Temple upkeep, and communal things go to communal gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Things given to be offered on the מזבח
Things given for the upkeep and repair of the Temple
Offerings that belong to the whole community
Communal gift offerings, brought when the מזבח is otherwise idle

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the money goes to gift offerings, and לוי says it buys קטורת. Each has a ברייתא supporting him. The general rule is that repayment money goes back to the same kind of holiness it came from.

phrases.english: All altar offerings: the money goes to the altar.

phrases.aramaic: קׇרְבְּנוֹת קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת – לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: Things given for Temple upkeep: the money goes to Temple upkeep.
Communal offerings: the money goes to communal gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא that supports רב closes with a general summary rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repayment money for מעילה goes back to the same kind of holiness: altar, Temple upkeep, or communal gift offerings.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the ברייתא sends leftover חטאת money to the ים המלח, but its closing rule says all altar-offering money goes to the מזבח, whether or not the owner already got atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. It first says: before his חטאת was brought, he adds the money and brings his חטאת. Once his חטאת was brought, the money goes to the ים המלח. But then it teaches that money from all altar offerings goes to the מזבח, with no difference whether the owner already got atonement or not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that two parts of the same ברייתא seem to clash. The first part and the closing rule seem to give different answers for the same money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, the ברייתא said חטאת money is thrown into the ים המלח once the חטאת was already brought. In step 10, it said all מעילה money from altar offerings goes to the מזבח. That general rule makes no exception for an owner who already got atonement, so it seems to cover the very case the first part sent to the ים המלח.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult: it seems to contradict itself
The owners already got their atonement

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to רב or לוי. The גמרא is now only checking that the ברייתא agrees with itself.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
before his sin offering was brought,
he adds and brings his sin offering;
phrases.notes: He adds this money to what he has and buys a better animal for his חטאת.

phrases.english: once his sin offering was brought,
the money goes to the Dead Sea.
But it teaches: all altar offerings go to the altar,
phrases.notes: This is the closing rule of the same ברייתא from step 10.

phrases.english: and there is no difference whether the owners achieved atonement
or where they did not achieve atonement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from using the ברייתא as proof to testing whether it agrees with itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא (steps 8 and 10)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general closing rule sends all altar-offering money to the מזבח without exception, which seems to contradict the first part sending already-atoned חטאת money to the ים המלח.

steps.title: The first part follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who rules that any חטאת whose owner already got atonement is left to die, so its money is destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part follows רבי שמעון, who says: any חטאת whose owners already got atonement is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two parts of the ברייתא follow different תנאים. The first part follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, a חטאת whose owner already got atonement cannot be used at all and is left to die. Its money is treated the same way, so it is thrown into the ים המלח. The closing rule, which sends all altar-offering money to the מזבח, does not follow this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
A חטאת whose owners already got atonement through a different animal
It is left to die; nobody may use it at all

steps.whatToRemember: The two parts of the ברייתא do not clash. The ים המלח rule follows רבי שמעון's view that a חטאת whose owner already got atonement is left to die.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: when one source seems to contradict itself, the different parts can follow different תנאים.

phrases.english: The first part follows Rabbi Shimon,
who says: any sin offering
whose owners achieved atonement is left to die.
phrases.notes: The owners got atonement through a different animal, so this one has no use left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two parts of the source to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא follows one view, so its first part and its closing rule contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part follows רבי שמעון, for whom an already-atoned חטאת is left to die, so its money goes to the ים המלח. The closing rule does not follow this view.
